chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus: that he presented the Book of Blood-Monies to Abi al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, and in it there was:

For the loss of hearing altogether, one thousand dinars. For the loss of the voice altogether due to nasalization and hoarseness, one thousand dinars. For paralysis in both hands, complete paralysis, one thousand dinars. For paralysis of the two legs, one thousand dinars. For the two lips, if they are completely removed, one thousand dinars. For the back, if it becomes hunchbacked, one thousand dinars. For the penis, if it is completely severed, one thousand dinars. For the two testicles, one thousand dinars. And concerning a man’s temple, if it is injured so that he is unable to turn except to the extent that the man is bent aside, then half of the diyah: five hundred dinars. Whatever is less than that is according to its calculation.

key_terms.الدِّيَاتِ: financial compensations prescribed for bodily injury or killing
key_terms.الشَّلَلِ: paralysis or permanent loss of function
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: a dinar, the monetary unit used for legal compensation
key_terms.صُدْغِ: the temple area of the head

ai.seo_question: What compensation is due in Shia fiqh for permanent bodily injuries such as loss of hearing, paralysis, or severance of organs?
ai.summary: This hadith records legal rulings on fixed compensations for severe bodily injuries in the law of diyah. It details amounts for total loss or permanent disabling harm to major organs and faculties, showing the structured assessment of bodily rights and injury compensation in Shia fiqh.
